questions.question: The origin of ‘Carnatic music’ is related to which of the following Dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayanagar **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayanagar Dynasty:-**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was a South Indian dynasty based in the Deccan Plateau region.
 
• **Established in 1336 by Harihara I and his brother Bukka Raya I of the Sangama Dynasty, the empire lasted until 1646, although its power declined after a major military defeat in 1565 by the Deccan sultanates.**
 
• The empire is named after its capital city of Vijayanagara, whose remains surround present-day Hampi, now a World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was divided into various eras based on the ruling dynasty: Sangama Dynasty (1336–1485), Saluva Dynasty (1485–1505), Tuluva Dynasty (1505–1570), and the Aravidu Dynasty (1570–1646).
 
• **The origin of ‘Carnatic music’ is related to this Dynasty.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bahmani Sultanate:-**

 
 
• It is also called the Bahmanid Empire.
 
• It was a Muslim state in Deccan, India that lasted from 1347 to 1527.
 
• The Sultanate was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah, a rebel officer who revolted against the Delhi Sultanate ruled by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq.
 
• After gaining independence, Alauddin took the title of 'Bahman Shah', which led to the dynasty being named "Bahmani".
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty:-**
 
 
• 
 
It was a Tamil dynasty that ruled primarily in southern India until the 13th century.

 
 
• 
 
It was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the world's history.

 
 
• 
 
The earliest datable references to the Chola are in inscriptions from the 3rd century BCE, left by Ashoka, of the Maurya Empire, and the dynasty continued to rule over varying territory until the 13th century CE.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Pandya Dynasty:-**

 
 
• 
 
It was also referred to as the Pandyas, an ancient Tamil dynasty that ruled extensive territories, at times including the large regions of South India, from their home base in Madurai.

 
 
• 
 
Historical records of the Pandyas trace back to the 3rd century BCE and they have been prominently referenced in the ancient Sangam Literature of the Tamil people.

• __**Tansen's Connection with Miracles**__

• According to legend, the renowned singer was capable of working many miracles through his voice. The emperor was contacted by the ministers, who begged him to persuade Tansen to sing the **Raga Deepak**,** a raga that was meant to start fire! **Tansen was instructed to light the lamps by singing after Akbar, who was eager to see the miracle, ordered his slaves to set a number of them. **When Tansen sang Raga Deepak, all of the lamps simultaneously lit up!**
 
• Tansen also performed other miracles, such as bringing rain by singing Raga **Megh Malhar.** According to legend, **Tansen used this particular raga shortly after Raga Deepak.** This is due to the fact that Raga Deepak raised the temperature while Raga Megh Malhar lowered it. Raga Deepak has been lost to time, however Raga Megh Malhar is still in existence now.
 
• 
 
**Tansen was renowned for using music to communicate with animals.** A ferocious elephant is supposed to have once been brought into Akbar's court. All expectations were placed in Tansen because no one else could tame the animal. **The elephant was calmed by the emperor's favourite singer's songs**, and he also inspired Akbar to ride on it, which according to stories, Akbar did.
